goal: Bound the autopilot discovery and authoring agent calls with the default wall-clock deadline so a stalled SDK stream is cancelled and surfaces a timeout outcome under the default config, rather than parking the daemon on a turn budget that never bounds wall time.

relevant: packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/invoker.py -- around line 213 the `async for msg in source` loop has no asyncio.wait_for, so only max_turns bounds it, not wall-clock

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_autopilot.py -- invoke_iteration call sites (~436 discovery, ~856 authoring); max_turns (60/8/120) is a turn budget, not a time budget; the cycle is a blocking asyncio.run
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_autopilot_discovery.py -- keep this suite green; mirror its invoke-iteration injection
constraints: Use the deadline primitive and resolved-config autopilot ceiling from the prerequisite tasks; do not invent a bespoke timeout.
Under default config the discovery/authoring agent call runs under a finite wall-clock ceiling; a stream that never yields a terminal message must be cancelled.
A timeout surfaces a distinguishable timeout outcome so the cycle does not park; the resolved default autopilot agent ceiling is non-null.
Do not require the SDK extra at import; the invoker already goes through the lazy SDK boundary -- keep it that way.
Add the pytest target so `uv run pytest -k autopilot_agent_deadline` selects it.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not modify or weaken assertions in the autopilot discovery/authoring tests.
Do not change the core harness, rubric, command-grader, or docker paths here.
Do not replace the max_turns turn budget -- the wall-clock bound is additive to it.
edge_cases: An invoke-iteration whose underlying stream never yields a terminal message is cancelled with a timeout-classified outcome in bounded wall time, under DEFAULT config.
A stream that streams forever without spending a turn must still be bounded (turn budget alone is insufficient).
A normally-completing cycle still completes (no false-positive timeout).
